description: Pywr-DRB is a Python water-management model of the Delaware River Basin. Its maintainers use Pywr to represent reservoirs, transbasin diversions, minimum-flow targets and other operating rules when assessing water availability and drought risk. Inputs are inflow series, demand and policy settings; outputs include major streamflows, reservoir storage and reliability measures over a user-selected period. The model is specific to the basin, while the README's 1983–1985 run is an example, not its only study period. MIT-licensed code and tutorials are free, and a versioned software DOI identifies the release. The repository can use National Water Model or other observed and simulated inflow sources, so results depend on those assumptions and the selected regulatory rules. It serves infrastructure operations and drought-planning simulations, not real-time control of the physical reservoirs. The catalogue's model-noaa-national-water-model is one possible inflow source named by the README; this review did not run their linkage. No data or model package was downloaded.
